use.reason: For the actual finite-rank group-ring coefficient, every finite quotient has finite H0. Thus its H0 images stabilize, giving Mittag-Leffler and zero lim1. The quotients by (2^a,(1+t)^(2^n)-1) and finite-group coefficient relations are cofinal with powers of the maximal ideal: the former quotient is finite local, hence has nilpotent maximal ideal; conversely its defining elements lie in any prescribed maximal-ideal power for sufficiently large a,n. Apply the source exact sequence to this cofinal system. The already proved norm compatibility supplies the compatible H1 elements; it is not supplied by this theorem. For K10 take R=Z_2[[Gamma]][G]=Z_2[[t]][G], where G is the fixed finite elementary abelian two-group, and take the free rank-two R-module T_2E tensor R with the actual continuous chi_0 psi kappa^(-1) action. R is a complete noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m generated by2,t and g-1 for g in G; its residue field is F_2. The actual finite quotients use J_(a,n)=(2^a,(1+t)^(2^n)-1). The quotient R/J_(a,n) is finite and local: modulo2 it is the group algebra of the finite two-group Gamma_n times G, whose augmentation ideal is nilpotent. Hence some power of m is contained in J_(a,n). Conversely J_(a,n) is contained in any prescribed m^k for a,n sufficiently large: 2^a is in m^k for a>=k, while for 1<=i<k the coefficient binomial(2^n,i) has valuation at least n-v_2(i), and terms of degree i>=k are already in m^k. Thus these ideals and the m-adic powers define cofinal filtrations. Use a diagonal cofinal sequence in a,n. Each H0 of the finite quotient coefficient is a subgroup of a finite module, so its images stabilize and lim1 H0 vanishes. Apply Corollary4.1.3 to the complete finite-type admissible R-module through this cofinal identification. Norm compatibility of the already supplied classes produces their inverse-limit element; the argument proves no new norm relation.

supplier.statement: For an admissible finite-type coefficient module T over the complete coefficient ring, continuous cohomology sits in the exact sequence0->lim1 H^(i-1)(G,T/m^nT)->H^i_cont(G,T)->lim H^i(G,T/m^nT)->0.

use.reason: Apply at each finite coefficient precision to the open normal cyclotomic subgroup. Section8.1.3 gives the integral permutation basis. Section8.1.6.3 identifies the commuting deck action by hU->h*g^(-1)U, exactly the inverse-deck convention after naming that group basis. The explicit Phi_n in K10 is then checked on that basis in the manuscript; Shapiro does not itself assert equivariance of an arbitrary weighted map. Section8.1.6.2 gives unnormalized coset projection for corestriction, not division by the index.

supplier.statement: For an open subgroup U of a profinite group G, evaluation at1 gives a quasi-isomorphism from continuous cochains with induced discrete coefficients to cochains of U; the induced module has the explicit permutation-module model, and corestriction corresponds to the coset projection.

use.reason: At finite coefficients the continuous cocycle and action factor through a finite quotient after shrinking an open normal subgroup contained in the extension subgroup. Regroup the finite coset sum by the inertia orbits on G/U; each orbit is represented by one double coset and contributes the conjugated restriction followed by corestriction from its stabilizer I intersect gUg^(-1). This is K7. Its stabilizer is the upper inertia for the corresponding place. If every upper restriction is zero, each summand is zero. No condition that inertia map is trivial is used.

supplier.statement: The finite coset sum in Section8.1.4 defines a cochain map inducing corestriction, independent of the chosen coset section up to homotopy; nested sections make corestriction transitive.

use.reason: Take the continuous homomorphism to be the inertia inclusion and U the cyclotomic subgroup. Its preimage is upper inertia; the finite cosets enumerate the primes above the given place. The source decomposition and commuting restriction diagram identify the local restrictions with the upper restrictions. A zero class therefore stays zero under the integral coefficient map Phi_n. The finite local decomposition introduces no character projector or index denominator.

supplier.statement: Restriction of an induced coefficient module along a continuous homomorphism decomposes over the finite cosets of the induced image, and the Shapiro maps commute with the resulting local restriction maps up to the specified homotopy.
